info.title: FAF APIs
info.description: This is a hosted REST API to the US Bureau of Transportation Statistics (BTS) Feight Analysis Framework (FAF) dataset. It has been developed by the Data To Insight Center (D2I) at Indiana University as part of the NSF ICICLE AI Institute and in collaboration with the US Bureau of Transportation Statistics.

get.description: commodity_total/ endpoint accepts a timeframe and an option specifying either state or region. It returns a CSV file detailing the difference between the tonnage of each commodity imported and exported from each area by year. Currently, this endpoint supports domestic trade only, with plans for future updates to include international import and export data related to the U.S.

parameters.name: option
parameters.description:
There are two options to put in this parameter:

* region : uses the region tables I.E. regional
* state: uses the state tables I.E. state

parameters.name: timeframe
parameters.description: The variable timeframe takes a list that can hold either one or two integer values for years, like the following [2017] or [2017,2025]. One year will give all the data stored for that year, while two years will give the value for those two years as well as each year in between the two.

post.description: POST request for Commodity_total with timeframe and option in body.

get.description: imports_exports_details/ takes in a region or state with a year or year frame and returns all exported commodities from that area. The endpoint returns the commodity type, the transportation type, the area the commodity was sent to, and the year's ton and value.

parameters.name: commodity
parameters.description:
The variable commodity takes a  string value corresponding to commodity names.
Each string value should match an existing commodity name stored in the database.

Example:
- "Coal" will give details for the commodity "Coal" only.

The string value provided should correspond exactly to the commodity names as they are stored in the database to retrieve accurate data.

parameters.name: destination
parameters.description:
The destination parameter accepts a string that must represent either a region, state, or an area outside of the U.S. The names corresponding to these options can be retrieved from the [NAME ENDPOINT].

Both destination and origin need to use either region, state, or one of the two can be an out of country area.

parameters.name: flow
parameters.description:
The variable flow takes a single string value that represents the type of flow, which can be one of the following:

- "domestic" – Represents a flow within the same country.
- "foreign-Import" – Represents a flow of goods coming into the country from abroad.
- "foreign-Export" – Represents a flow of goods leaving the country to be exported abroad.

Only one of these string values should be provided at a time.

Example:
- "domestic" will provide data related to goods or services that are within the same country.
- "foreign-Export" will provide data related to goods or services leaving the country.

The string value provided must exactly match one of these options to retrieve the appropriate data.

parameters.name: origin
parameters.description:
The origin parameter accepts a string that must represent either a region, state, or an area outside of the U.S. The names corresponding to these options can be retrieved from the [NAME ENDPOINT].

Both destination and origin need to use either region, state, or one of the two can be an out of country area.

parameters.name: timeframe
parameters.description: The variable timeframe takes a list that can hold either one or two integer values for years, like the following [2017] or [2017,2025]. One year will give all the data stored for that year, while two years will give the value for those two years as well as each year in between the two.

parameters.name: transpotation
parameters.description:
The variable transportation takes a string value corresponding to transport modes, like the following Truck, Air, Water
Each string value should match an existing transport mode stored in the database.

Example:
- Truck will give details for the transport mode "Truck" only.

The string value provided should correspond exactly to the transport mode names as they are stored in the database to retrieve accurate data.

post.description: get_table_data/ retrieves one of six fully populated tables based on the year timeframe provided. The return is a downloadable CSV file. The data will contain the origin, destination, commodity type, transportation type, distance traveled, tonnage, and value based on the timeframe provided.

parameters.name: table
parameters.description:
The tables follow the naming convention of "faf" or "state" followed by 0, 1, 2, or 3, which describe the meaning of each table. FAF tables use regions, while state tables use U.S. states.

* 0 indicates that the table includes all movements of commodities between states, including those entering or leaving the U.S.

* 1 means the commodities are transported only within the U.S.

* 2 shows imported commodities into the U.S.

* 3 shows exported commodities from the U.S.

Hence the options for table are: faf0, faf1, faf2, faf3, state0, state1, state2, state3

post.description:
import_export_sum/ takes a region or state and a timeframe, then sums up each commodity
imported and exported from the origin separately for each year. This endpoint returns a CSV file containing the name of the origin, the commodity type if it is imported or exported, and the tonnage per year. Currently, this endpoint only works with domestic-traded commodities.

get.description:
Returns a CAV file detailing all one-way trade between two specified locations. The data includes:

* Origin to Destination: Indicates the direction of trade.

* Commodity: Specity unique commodities or use "all" to include all commodities. 

* Timeframe: Specify the year to filter the data accordingly.

Retrieves the transportation method, the tonnage, and the value of each commodity traded.

parameters.name: commodity
parameters.description: The commodity parameter accepts a string specifying the desired commodity. If "all" is used, the endpoint will return data for all commodities sent from the origin to the destination.
